PR-1: When the vendor creates a tenant, the system shall create one brand and one legal entity with at least one branch, and isolate all tenant data from every other tenant
PR-2: The owner shall manage branches (address, structured opening hours, closures, timezone, rooms, devices, services offered, optional WhatsApp number, map link, publish window) from one branch master
PR-3: Staff shall sign in with individual accounts; owner, Admin Pusat, manager, doctor, finance, facility head, records officer, internal auditor and central CS require a second factor (IAM-1); idle front-desk sessions lock
PR-4: The system shall record purpose-specific consents (care notice, procedure, internal clinical photo, marketing WhatsApp, publication) with history and withdrawal
PR-5: Front office shall register a patient with minimum identity (name, phone, date of birth, NIK or an official no-NIK identity type with reason, religion, occupation, education, marital status), record a guardian for minors, and resolve duplicates by explicit decision; one phone may belong to several patients without exposing each other's data
PR-6: Staff and the public booking link shall book a service at a branch, reserving only the resources the service requires, recording channel and source, and applying optional booking DP
PR-7: Front office shall check a patient in, open one visit, and see a live board with independent states (intake, doctor, selection, consent, payment, preparation, treatment, dispensing, closure) and an always-visible outstanding-payments list
PR-8: The lateness rule (release slot after N minutes) shall be a tenant setting, default off
PR-9: A BC shall record intake, photos and "Observasi Kulit" (chips and text only, no grades, scores or Fitzpatrick type) as unverified data, never a diagnosis, and see prior visits as history
PR-10: A doctor shall verify intake without retyping, examine, annotate the face map, and create or update a staged care plan, with prior visits, photos and plans visible on the same screen
PR-11: Treatment shall start only with valid practitioner credentials, competence, no unresolved contraindication, and consent matching the planned items and doses
PR-12: The system shall apply BILL-4 (consultation fee charged when nothing is bought, waived with a qualifying purchase on that visit, no retroactive waiver, re-charged from a full refund of all qualifying purchases) and BILL-5 (free controls per item, default one, valid to control date + 7 days)
PR-13: Signed clinical records shall be immutable; corrections within 2×24 h by the author create a new version; later administrative corrections need records-officer or facility-head approval; records are retained at least 25 years from the last visit; patients can receive a copy of record content
PR-14: Treatment staff shall work from a checklist that records start, actual performer, actual materials, and outcome: completed, medical stop, clinic-caused stop, or patient-chosen stop; medical or clinic stops do not use the session and allow free reschedule or move the payment to balance; a patient stop counts as used
PR-15: An additional treatment shall start only after patient and authorized clinician agreement recorded in the system; FO/cashier may release it before payment (recorded with the staff accountable for collection; no amount limit, no manager approval); FO is alerted at approval and again when it finishes unpaid; a visit cannot close with an unpaid bill or pending dispensing; after the WhatsApp-bill fallback FO may convert the remainder to a patient receivable, which settles the visit bill
PR-16: Material demand shall follow request → issue → consume / return / waste per item class; recommendation or selection never changes stock; nothing is deducted twice
PR-17: Stock shall be held per branch with batches, expiry, opened-vial use-by, FEFO, minimum/target levels, purchasing and goods receipt, inter-branch transfers, and counts
PR-18: The pharmacist shall receive an automatic preparation list from approved selections and dispense prescriptions and products after the seven pharmacist checks (CD-19: patient and prescriber identity, prescription validity, dose/route/frequency, allergy and interaction check, clarification outcome, label, counselling) recorded with dispenser identity and exceptions; batch-to-patient traceability; stock in `quarantined`, `recalled` or `temperature_excursion` status is non-dispensable until released by the pharmacist with reason; recalls list affected dispensings; special drugs (narcotics, psychotropics) are excluded and cannot be enabled until their controls are approved; external-use label where required (verify Permenkes 34/2021 scope with Numa's pharmacist)
PR-19: The cashier shall issue invoices with frozen prices, accept split tender (cash, QRIS, EDC, transfer, payment link, patient balance), allocate partial payments proportionally after discount, print/send receipts, sell products at the counter without a visit (patient optional; pharmacist hand-over still required for regulated items), void an invoice only through approval (requester ≠ approver), and close shifts with any non-zero cash variance approved (BILL-18)
PR-20: Packages shall unlock sessions only within cumulative paid value using the decided session-value rule, accept installments without a binding schedule or interest (an optional reminder-only schedule, PR-96, creates no debt or entitlement), enforce minimum DP and validity, reserve a session at booking/check-in and redeem it only when the outcome counts (B-15), and on expiry or cancellation move paid-unused value to patient balance and cancel the unpaid remainder
PR-21: Patient balance shall never expire, pay for any item, and be refunded in cash only as an approved, recorded exception
PR-22: Booking DP shall be applied on arrival, move to balance on patient change ≥ 24 h, be forfeited on no-show or patient change < 24 h, and on clinic cancellation move to balance or be refunded if the patient asks
PR-23: Commissions shall follow BILL-15 (role default + individual override, % or fixed, actual allocated payment basis, guiding/closing BC, new patient on first visit, performer only when counted, monthly approval, refund and moved-to-balance adjustments, carry-forward of excess deductions, rule snapshots, no commission on written-off items or top-ups); staff see only their own; per-recipient commission export for the tax adviser
PR-24: Each sellable item shall carry a tax category with a recorded basis; invoices snapshot it; VAT applies only while the tenant is PKP and only after the tax adviser's written advice (Q-05) is recorded; consumer prices are VAT-inclusive; a 12-month turnover monitor warns non-PKP tenants near Rp4.8 billion
PR-25: Accounting step 1 shall keep sub-ledgers for cash/bank by method, contract liability (paid not yet delivered), receivables, patient balance, package liability, booking DP, commission payable and VAT, with roll-forward reports and sub-ledger/transaction CSV exports (journal export only after the posting map is signed, A-14)
PR-26: Accounting (step 2, Release 1) shall provide a chart of accounts, automatic posting from events per an approved posting map, manual journals, period lock, trial balance, P&L, balance sheet and cash-flow summary (P&L per branch and consolidated; balance sheet per branch through inter-branch clearing), for SAK EMKM or SAK EP
PR-27: The vendor shall onboard each tenant's WhatsApp Business Account through Embedded Signup (incl. Coexistence), with numbers per branch or per brand and `Brand – Branch` display names, tracking registration, display-name status, quality and the portfolio messaging limit; a BSP fallback is used if our Tech Provider approval is pending (W-09)
PR-28: Staff shall work one shared WhatsApp inbox per tenant with branch routing, assignment, service-window timer, quick replies and template sending
PR-29: Leads shall follow new → contacted → booked → arrived → converted / lost (reason), with source, campaign and first-response time
PR-30: The system shall create follow-up tasks from decided rules (control due, next package stage, package expiry 30/14/7 days, locked installment sessions, receivables, unselected plan items, no-shows, dormant > 90 days)
PR-31: Outbound messages shall respect consent, a tenant-level daily budget under the shared messaging limit, and carry no diagnosis, treatment detail or photos
PR-32: Clinical photos and documents shall be private, served through short-lived authenticated access, and kept separate from publication rights
PR-33: Role dashboards shall show the KPIs of Appendix A for their role (PR-33a–PR-33f) with branch and consolidated views, each value drilling down to the records behind it, without clinical content
PR-34: A reconciliation report shall show differences between operational KPIs and ledger balances by day and branch
PR-35: Signed clinical events shall be sent to SATUSEHAT through a durable outbox per branch credentials, with retries, error list and monitoring; outages never block local care; non-medical BC intake is not sent as a clinician finding
PR-36: Production storage locations (database, object storage, backups, logs, error tracking) shall be read from deployed configuration and declared in the vendor profile; real-patient go-live (tenant activation, patient creation, public booking in production) is blocked until the residency-opinion flag (H-02d) is set or all locations are Indonesian; a migration runbook moves the whole environment (not a single tenant) to another region without code changes
PR-37: Approvals (refund exception, write-off, attribution correction, commission batch, stock adjustment, disposal) shall use requester ≠ approver and be audited, except an owner-initiated write-off (B-14), which needs a mandatory reason and is audited
PR-38: Tenant settings shall be a registry (`19` §5, SET-1–SET-49): each setting has a researched default, type and bounds, tenant or branch scope, the roles that may change it, an effective date and an audit record; transactions snapshot the value used; "Kembalikan ke default" restores the research default; class F rules (law, money integrity, isolation) are never settings; adding a setting needs a decision
PR-39: Public pages shall load no session replay and no third-party ad or analytics pixel on any treatment, concern, doctor, booking, intake or complaint route (these URLs reveal health intent); only the home and branch pages may load a marketing pixel, after consent, with path and query redaction
PR-40: Rich public content (educational articles with medical-review stamp, consented before/after only if counsel clears it under Permenkes 1787/2010 Pasal 5, concern landings, skin quiz, display-only product catalog) shall extend the basic public site (PR-64); **no patient testimonials on public pages** (Pasal 5 huruf n)
PR-41: The owner and manager shall maintain one versioned catalog of services, products, packages and material formulas with per-item control rules, booking-DP flag, tax category, commission scope and normal price; clinical fields (indications, contraindications, consent template, delegation) publish only after clinical-lead review
PR-42: The owner shall set branch price overrides on the shared catalog; invoices snapshot the branch-effective price; package session value uses the selling branch's effective normal prices at sale time
PR-43: Staff shall flag an inbound message or visit note either as **Klinis** (suspected complication or adverse event → clinical review task for the branch's clinician on duty, response target CD-33) or **Layanan** (waiting time, billing dispute, staff behaviour → task for the branch manager, response target CD-40), each with status; treatment-caused extra controls are free
PR-44: One approvals inbox shall list every approval type (refund exception, write-off, attribution and guiding-BC reassignment, commission batch, stock adjustment, disposal, late record correction, shift variance, invoice void, manual discount above limit) with requester ≠ approver (owner write-off exception, PR-37)
PR-45: Clinicians shall receive and decide clinical requests (additional treatment, plan change, substitution) from the room or BC on their phone or iPad, with reason on decline
PR-46: Inventory shall be valued at moving average cost per item per branch; consumption, waste and transfers post at that cost; margin reports label estimated consumption
PR-47: The owner shall set BC targets (closing value per month, plans fully selected) and staff see attainment in Saya
PR-48: Managers shall maintain staff schedules (shifts, leave) per branch; booking offers only rostered performers
PR-49: A patient profile shall show identity, contacts, guardian, consents (with withdrawal), balance, packages and receivables, and produce a copy of record content for the patient
PR-50: Data-subject requests shall be logged and tracked to closure with due dates
PR-51: The owner and facility head shall review an audit log of clinical access, break-glass use, approvals and settings changes
PR-52: The owner shall export all tenant data (clinical as FHIR bundle + PDF per record, financial and CRM as CSV) with a checksum manifest, for exit and handover
PR-53: The vendor operator console shall provision tenants and open time-limited, reasoned, tenant-visible support sessions
PR-54: In-app notifications shall deliver role alerts (unpaid addition, clinical request, complaint task, approval waiting) with acknowledgement
PR-55: The vendor operator shall maintain a vendor profile (legal name, NIB, PSE number, NPWP, Meta business ID, website, privacy-policy URL, support contacts, declared storage locations, residency-opinion reference/date/outcome/set-by with file checksum) used by receipts, templates, legal pages and registrations; placeholder values are visibly marked and block production go-live until replaced; only the product owner may set the residency-opinion flag, audited
PR-56: The vendor shall manage each tenant through lifecycle states provisioning → onboarding → live → suspended → exit → closed, with reason and owner notice on suspend and exit; suspension is manual and reversible by the platform owner with reason; while suspended, new bookings, public pages and marketing stop, while existing appointments, cashier, care messages (aftercare, reminders for existing bookings, complaint replies) and clinical read/export continue
PR-57: Vendor staff shall hold vendor roles (platform owner, onboarding, support, vendor finance, auditor) separate from clinic memberships, with TOTP and requester ≠ approver for clinical-data grants, suspension, exit, server-fee change and invoice waiver
PR-58: An onboarding grant shall let onboarding staff configure branches, catalog, staff invitations, imports and branding until go-live or 30 days (renewable once by the owner in Akses Vendor), never clinical rows, visible to the owner
PR-59: The processor agreement and NDA shall be signed before onboarding starts (TEN-12); go-live shall require every blocking onboarding-checklist item per tenant and branch (entity and tax status, branches, catalog, staff and credentials, money settings; payment port, WABA and SATUSEHAT when used) and the platform owner's confirmation; the go-live date starts server-fee billing
PR-60: Platform-level vendor views shall show counts and status codes only; clinic data is reachable only in a support session (PR-53) that the owner sees in Saya › Akses Vendor, can end, and must approve first when the scope includes clinical data or specific personal data (TEN-14); every record read in a session is listed to the owner; infrastructure access (SEC-20) is reported the same way
PR-61: The vendor shall bill each live tenant a monthly server fee (default Rp1,000,000, VAT-exclusive, set per tenant with reason and effective month, approved by the platform owner), invoiced per BILL-31 (prorated first month, then monthly in advance due on the 10th; waiver and credit notes as new documents), paid by QRIS/VA through the vendor's AutoLaris account using payment attempts per BILL-32, and marked paid only by the AutoLaris Advice status confirmed for the account (Q-13); reminders at due date, +7 and +14 days
PR-62: The vendor console shall show platform health per tenant and provider (uptime, worker heartbeat, outbox backlog, backup age, error rate) from existing telemetry, without clinic content (error codes and counts only; provider error bodies never shown outside a session)
PR-63: The tenant shall support Admin Pusat (tenant-wide configuration of branches, catalog, staff, settings drafts and public site; not branch price overrides, cash-refund or write-off approval, commission batch approval, tenant export or vendor-access approval), Marketing (promos, public-site content, lead-source reports; consented contacts only; no clinical data), Purchasing (suppliers, POs, receipts, transfers, supplier returns, stock reports across branches) and Internal auditor (read-only audit log, approvals, suspicious-activity, stock variance, refunds and write-offs)
PR-64: Each tenant shall have a basic public site generated from branch master, catalog and staff profiles (home, treatments, treatment detail, branches, branch detail, doctors, doctor profile, booking, privacy, terms, cancellation policy; no promo page until Q-15), published by owner, Admin Pusat or Marketing, served on the booking host at a slug path until domain routing is activated
PR-65: Public pages shall follow Permenkes 1787/2010 (JUR-ID-7): accurate, evidence-based, informative, educational (Pasal 4); no superlatives or "satu-satunya", no comparison with other clinics, no promised or unrealistic results, no testimonials, no **advertised discounts or sales promotions**, no academic or professional titles used as promotion (Pasal 5 huruf b–e, m, n, o); treatment pages show what it is for, who performs it, duration, downtime, sessions and interval, and the branch-effective tariff only when published (otherwise "Harga dijelaskan saat konsultasi"); clinical text publishes only after clinical-lead review
PR-66: Doctors shall appear on the public site only with recorded listing consent, as factual information (name, practice schedule, branch, SIP status as the clinic chooses), never as a model or endorser (Permenkes 1787/2010 Pasal 8); whether titles may be shown is confirmed by counsel (Q-15); withdrawal hides them on the next publish
PR-67: Every public page shall offer booking with treatment, branch or doctor prefilled and a labelled WhatsApp link carrying a source tag; unpublished or suspended tenants return not-found or a closed notice with no tenant data
PR-68: Patient payments by QRIS, virtual account or payment link shall go through one payment port (create charge, status, cancel, refund where supported, channel list, webhook verification) with normalized states; Release 1 ships a mock adapter that simulates paid, expired, failed, duplicate and late webhooks, marks its receipts SIMULASI and never counts as cash; a real provider is one adapter chosen per tenant (Q-14); cash, EDC and manual transfer need no gateway
PR-69: The system shall send appointment reminders (default H-1 and same-day morning, branch setting) as neutral WhatsApp utility templates (clinic, branch, date and time; no service name, PRIV-15) with Konfirmasi and Ubah Jadwal replies that update the appointment, within the outbound budget
PR-70: Each catalog item may carry clinical-reviewed aftercare text delivered at visit close as a care message (not marketing): a neutral WhatsApp notice with a short-lived OTP-protected link, or printed at the clinic (PRIV-15); a reply reporting a problem is offered to staff as a complaint flag (PR-43)
PR-71: Front office shall register walk-in patients without a booking from Hari Ini and issue a daily queue number per branch; a TV call display is optional
PR-72: Manual discounts shall have a limit per role (percent and rupiah, tenant setting); above the limit the discount waits in Persetujuan; every manual discount appears in the suspicious-activity report
PR-73: Clinical credentials (STR, SIP, SIPP, SIPA) shall raise alerts, only for credentials that carry an expiry date (lifetime STR has none), to the holder and the facility head 60, 30 and 7 days before expiry and appear in Perlu Ditangani
PR-74: The tenant shall maintain versioned templates for receipts, procedure consent and medical letters (surat keterangan, rujukan, resume); letters are created from a template, signed by the doctor and stored as part of the medical record
PR-75: Purchasing shall maintain suppliers and record supplier returns with reason, batch and credit note, reducing stock at moving average cost
PR-76: Roles with patient-identity access (07) shall search patients by name, phone, medical-record number and invoice number from their role home; search runs in PostgreSQL under RLS (no external index); results show name, masked phone, MRN and status only for allowed branches; invoice results show totals, not line items, to non-clinical roles; queries are sent in the request body, excluded from logs, rate-limited per staff, and more than the hourly threshold alerts the facility head
PR-77: Promo and voucher codes with quota, period, eligible items and branches, and usage statistics, applied as discount lines **at the cashier and in direct consented messages only**; discounts are never advertised on public pages (Permenkes 1787/2010 Pasal 5 huruf m)
PR-78: Post-visit satisfaction survey; a low score creates a manager task before any public review request
PR-79: Operational expenses and petty cash per branch with category and receipt photo, feeding branch margin and accounting step 2
PR-80: Daily owner digest by WhatsApp or email (cash in, completed service, exceptions), aggregates only
PR-81: Waitlist for a service and branch when no slot is free, offered when a slot opens
PR-82: Device and room logbooks (sterilization, calibration, maintenance) and a patient-safety incident register (KTD, KNC, KTC, KPC, sentinel) with responsible officer, classification, immediate response, investigation, reporting determination (recipient and deadline only as verified), submission evidence and corrective-action closure; medical-waste register link (date, category, quantity, authorized handler, handover evidence) without a waste-logistics module (Permenkes 11/2017 Pasal 5; PP 28/2024; PP 22/2021 — verify)
PR-83: Front office and CS shall manage appointments by state (booked, confirmed, arrived, no-show, cancelled, rescheduled) with actions Ubah Jadwal, Batalkan and Tandai Tidak Datang, view the calendar by doctor, room or device, and receive a task for every "Ubah Jadwal" reminder reply; booking-DP rules apply (PR-22)
PR-84: Staff with several allowed branches or several memberships shall switch the active branch (Saya › Ganti Cabang) and brand (Saya › Ganti Klinik); the active brand and branch are shown under the title and recorded on every action
PR-85: Records officers shall merge duplicate patients with an audited, reversible merge record; onboarding staff shall import patients, packages and balances through a validated CSV import with dry-run report (MIG-3)
PR-86: The clinic app shall present the complete research-based navigation tree of `19` §2 (dashboard, front office, schedule, patients, clinical, treatment room, cashier, packages, pharmacy and inventory, staff, marketing and CRM, finance, reports, approvals and audit, integrations, settings, Saya) with the global shell (branch switcher, global search, quick actions, notifications, inbox badge, user menu), role-filtered (pages a role cannot use are absent), with list and detail page conventions NAV-4 and NAV-5
PR-87: The vendor console shall present the complete tree of `19` §3, and the public site the page set of `19` §4
PR-88: The tenant shall maintain a service master (Master Layanan): category, duration (prep 0–120, treatment 5–480, buffer 0–120 min), required room/device, eligible staff and delegation, branch price, tax class, BHP recipe with units, consent template, aftercare text, online-bookable flag and web fields; clinical fields publish after facility-head review; materials by pharmacist
PR-89: Stock shall be held per depot within a branch (e.g. gudang, ruang tindakan, apotek) with transfers between depots and between branches, and alerts for low stock, near expiry and opened-vial use-by
PR-90: Purchasing shall record supplier invoices against goods receipts, track supplier payables (due date, balance), record payments to suppliers and apply supplier credit notes
PR-91: The tenant shall see and manage access: a read-only permission matrix per role (07), active sessions per staff with revoke, duty assignments (data protection, IT admin), and a log of permission changes
PR-92: The tenant shall keep a privacy workspace: consent purposes and texts (versioned), consent ledger across patients, processor register, breach register with notice evidence, and data-subject requests (PR-50)
PR-93: Patient packages may be shared with named family beneficiaries only where the owner enables it per package template (default off, B-03 keeps no sharing until enabled); swaps are value-based with doctor approval
PR-94: CRM automation scenarios: reminders (H-3, H-1, same day), post-treatment follow-up (H+1, H+7, H+14), control due, package expiry, product refill, birthday greeting (care-neutral text, marketing consent), dormant reactivation; each scenario has an on/off, offsets and a frequency cap per patient
PR-95: Reports shall include, besides K1–K19: average ticket, churn, top patients by spend, lifetime value, sales per shift, doctor activity (visits, unsigned records), pharmacy waiting time, promo-code performance and satisfaction; defined as K20–K27 in Appendix A (versioned in the KPI dictionary); every report links its definition in the KPI dictionary page
PR-96: Instalment schedules on receivables and packages may be recorded optionally (agreed dates and amounts) for reminders only; payments still unlock sessions by paid value (B-03)
PR-97: Experts do not get logins. Their output enters as evidence in a compliance register (vendor level: PSE, residency opinion H-02d, SATUSEHAT vendor registration, Meta, processor-agreement template; tenant level: tax advice, accountant posting-map sign-off, clinical authority matrix, SOPs for downtime, incidents and waste, DPIA, DPO/Penanggung Jawab/pharmacist appointments, signed processor agreement); each item has owner, status, date, file with checksum, validity and the features it unlocks; features gated by an item (VAT on invoices, journal export, public-site publish, campaign sending, clinical go-live, real-patient go-live) stay off until the item is approved
PR-98: PKP tenants shall export output-tax invoices as Coretax XML per month from frozen invoice tax snapshots, with corrections and returns as their own documents; the export is available only after the tax-advice evidence is approved (PR-97)
PR-33a: Owner dashboard (Ringkasan): Perlu Ditangani, K1, K2, K3, K4, K5 with package-expiry slice, K6, K1 vs K2 trend, branch league (K1, K2, K7, K8, K9, K10, K11, K12, K16, K17), treatment mix (K2, K7), channel funnel (K13); deltas compare with the tenant's own previous period (D-11)
PR-33b: Branch manager dashboard: today counts, chase list, tomorrow gaps (K15), stock risk (K18), staff (K19, K17)
PR-33c: Front office: Hari Ini board plus shift summary by tender
PR-33d: BC: my patients, follow-ups due, own K19 and K17
PR-33e: CS: inbox health (new, unassigned, overdue K14), K13 by source
PR-33f: Finance: K1 by method, K3, K4 aging, K5 detail, K6, refunds/write-offs, commission batches, roll-forwards
PR-33g: Admin Pusat home: setup completeness per branch (hours, rooms, catalog prices, staff and credentials), pending configuration and approvals routed to the owner, branch status list
